signals.summary: Hyrox, the standardized functional-fitness race (sled pushes, wall balls, SkiErg, sandbags, rowers in arena format), keeps spreading globally from Germany to China. The imagery is gear-and-arena led: branded stations, chalk, sleds and turf lanes.
signals.why_now: 5 independent outlets in the window — DW (100h), The Times (122h), ABC News (246h), Yahoo (244h), plus Times of India competitive-fitness angle (108h) — sustained global craze coverage.

signals.summary: Wave of interest in morning sunlight exposure and light-hygiene as the anchor of a wellness routine — sun through windows, early-day outdoor light, and the quiet walk-back of blue-light panic. Purely environment-led: morning light on interiors, a mat by the window, a mug in the sun.
signals.why_now: Fresh science-and-routine coverage: PsyPost on morning sunlight and earlier sleep (88h), BGR debunking blue-light-on-sleep fears (71h), reinforced by evergreen morning-yoga content (Yoga With Adriene). Cross-source and squarely seasonal/evergreen.

signals.summary: Home-workout gear as the object of desire — power racks, Smith machines, compact rowers, ellipticals — as home-workout demand ticks up again. Strongly object/interior led: a garage or spare-room setup, racked plates, a rower against a wall.
signals.why_now: Recent news of home fitness-equipment sales climbing (Hürriyet, 9h) sits atop a deep evergreen gear-review base (Breaking Muscle power racks, rowers, ellipticals, Smith machines). Object-first and highly producible.

signals.summary: A cluster of trends pushing back on grind culture: exercise 'snacks', 'doing less', intuitive workouts, and ultra-slow running. Producible through environment cues — a stair landing, a park path, a mat beside a desk — rather than intense demos.
signals.why_now: Four independent outlets in-window: Us Weekly on exercise snacks (65h), WION on intuitive workouts (414h), Canadian Running on Korea's viral slow-running (112h), ELLE on the do-less workout. Distinct sources converging on one mood.

signals.summary: Heat-based recovery — outdoor saunas, infrared rooms, and the back-to-basics recovery conversation — as a warm, textural wellness ritual. Interior/object led: cedar-lined sauna, steam, coals, a robe on a hook.
signals.why_now: Multiple angles surfacing: The Conversation on infrared workouts (582h), Medical Xpress on what actually works in recovery, and evergreen outdoor-sauna gear coverage; heading into cooler-season heat-ritual demand.

signals.summary: Strength and functional-movement work is displacing weight-loss as the stated gym goal, reframed around aging well and staying independent. Best served object-led: a rack of dumbbells, a resistance band, a barbell on a mat, rather than body demos.
signals.why_now: Several outlets converge: Yahoo on strength training overtaking weight-loss as top goal (186h), NYT on PT exercises to age well (143h), Tom's Guide on functional-strength moves for seniors (126h), plus HN squats discussion (21h).
